**4.** **Analysis** **parameters**

Table 3 summarizes the comparative study parameters. To determine the turbopump power density, some case studies were
performed using practical data. Fig. 8 plots the power densities of
turbopumps using LOX/kerosene propellant. For the GG cycle only,
the majority of the turbopumps (indicated by dashed-box) have
power densities between 11 kW/kg and 16 kW/kg. Their mean
value is 13.5 kW/kg with a standard deviation of 1.5 kW/kg. In
this study, a value of 13.5 kW/kg is adopted. For the pump power
densities of the ElecPump cycle, the values of 20 kW/kg for the
LOX pump and 15 kW/kg for the fuel pump are taken from the
authors’ research group reference data. In the GG cycle turbopumps, most turbines are single or dual-stage supersonic impulse
turbines because of their high pressure ratio (whereas reaction turbines are usually employed for staged-combustion cycles). Thus a
single-stage supersonic impulse turbine is used, as described in
Section 3.1.2. Considering the temperature limit of turbine material
(INCO 718), the turbine inlet temperature is assumed to be 900 K.
The efficiency of the turbine is also assumed to have a value of 52%
from historical data [40]. The exhausted gas properties from the
GG are determined from an empirical formulation. The GG pressure is assumed to be the same as the combustion chamber pressure ( _pcc_ ). The LOX pump and fuel pump efficiencies are 66% and
61%, respectively. For the motor, a maximum value of 5.8 kW/kg
for the power density and 96% efficiency were reported for the
state-of-the-art PM motor [41]. In this study, a power density of
5.3 kW/kg and 95% efficiency were chosen. The inverter properties
are assumed to be the same as in the preceding study [18]. For the
battery pack, the properties of the D cell are used. Helium is considered with an initial pressure of 27.0 MPaA and temperature of
100 K for the pressurizing gas. Titanium alloy, Ti-6AL-4V, is chosen
for the helium tank material. For the propellant tanks and GG, an
aluminum alloy and INCONEL 718 are used, respectively.

To determine a mass flow rate in a combustion chamber with
respect to thrust level, the characteristic velocity ( _c_ <sup>∗</sup> ) and thrust
coefficient ( _C F_ ) are calculated as a function of combustion chamber pressure ( _pcc_ ) using CEA [42]. The nozzle exit pressure is set to
0.002 MPaA in the calculations, considering the final stage application of a launch vehicle. Finally, the required pump outlet pressures
are assumed to be 115% for the LOX pump and 155% for the fuel
pump with respect to combustion chamber pressure.

**5.** **Results**

_5.1._ _Basic_ _features_

In this section, the ElecPump cycle is analyzed in terms of mass
for application to a final stage with a thrust range of 25–100 kN.
One important feature of a final stage is that the initial mass itself should be as low as possible, because this mass is a payload of
the lower stages. Fig. 9 shows the initial ElecPump cycle mass ratio
to GG cycle as a function of combustion chamber pressure. For a
shorter burning time of 300 s, the ElecPump cycle weighs more
than the GG cycle, primarily because the battery pack is heavier than the propellant consumed by the GG. A shorter burning
time leads to less available battery cell energy, and consequently
increases the mass of the battery pack. However, the initial mass
of the ElecPump cycle is from 0.2% to 1.3% lighter than that of
GG cycle for a longer burning time of 1200 s. In these cases, the
propellant for the GG has a higher mass than the battery pack.
The higher energy efficiency of the battery cell for long discharge

times also contributes to this advantages. Recalling that the definitions of the initial mass in each cycle in Eq. (4) and Eq. (30)
do not include valves, pipelines, and other structural masses, this
advantage would be further increased if the mass analysis were
expanded to the stage level in detail, because the ElecPump cycle
has fewer components than the GG cycle. To examine this phenomenon in depth, the initial mass budgets are analyzed. Three
cases are demonstrated ( _m_ <sup>0</sup> _EP_ <sup>_> m_</sup> _GG_ <sup>0</sup> <sup>,</sup> <sup>_m_</sup> <sup>0</sup> _EP_ <sup>=</sup> <sup>_m_</sup> _GG_ <sup>0</sup> <sup>,</sup> <sup>and</sup> <sup>_m_</sup> <sup>0</sup> _EP_ <sup>_< m_</sup> _GG_ <sup>0</sup> <sup>),</sup>
